guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: huge sludgy drum-mic guitar with room thump
tone.profile: huge sludgy drum-mic guitar with room thump
tone.summary: A heavy, saturated signal chain using Distortion for grit, followed by a powerful British amp model (UK 800) to deliver the necessary low-end thump, finished with a large Room reverb and EQ shaping for darkness.

rig.name: Led Zeppelin - When The Levee Breaks - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up low-end rumble and excessive noise inherent in sludgy tones.
Provide the required dirty saturation and thick sustain without resorting to aggressive fuzz.
blocks.gap: The 'Distortion' model is used as a general dirt source, mimicking heavy tube breakup rather than specific overdrive tones.

blocks.purpose: Slightly push the signal into the amp to maximize low-end girth and sustain.
blocks.gap: A dedicated boost is used primarily for volume lift and saturation enhancement, rather than tone shaping.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the massive low-end thump and dark character required for a sludgy, heavy tone.
blocks.gap: The UK 800 is chosen for its powerful bass response, fitting the 'low-tuned boom' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Provide a solid, full-bodied foundation that complements the low-end focus of the UK 800.
blocks.gap: The specific cabinet choice is less critical than the amp/IR combination, but this provides necessary body.

blocks.purpose: Darken the top end and tame harsh mids while maintaining low-end weight, fulfilling the 'dark top end' requirement.
blocks.gap: Used for surgical tone shaping to achieve a dark, massive sound profile.

blocks.purpose: Bypass (No Wah needed for this sludgy tone).
Create the required 'big room ambience' and sense of space for the massive tone.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is ideal for simulating a large, natural acoustic environment.

blocks.purpose: Bypass (No noticeable delay needed for the core sludgy tone).
Overall output level adjustment to ensure the 'huge' impact of the tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and low-end definition using an IR to better capture the 'drum-mic' room thump.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Large Room Impulse Response (e.g., large hall or drum kit mic)
proposals.reason: Enhance the perceived 'drum-mic' room thump and massive ambience.
